exemplar.title: What strong work looks like
exemplar.intro: A strong data-detective report interprets every statistic — here is how one student analyzed a books-read-per-month survey.

traits.sample: I asked 'How many books do sixth graders read each month?' — it expects many different answers, which is what makes it statistical.
traits.why: It names the variability that a statistical question requires.

traits.trait: Interprets center, not just computes it
traits.sample: The median of 3 books beats the mean of 4.1 here, because two super-readers with 15 books pull the mean up.
traits.why: The measure of center is chosen and defended, not just calculated.

traits.sample: A MAD of 1.8 means a typical student is about 2 books away from the mean — our class reads pretty similarly.
traits.why: The MAD is translated into plain language about the group.

traits.trait: Tests the effect of an outlier
traits.sample: When I added a reader with 30 books, the mean jumped from 4.1 to 5.6 but the median only moved from 3 to 3.5.
traits.why: It shows, with numbers, why medians resist outliers.
